1. Heard Sri T.S. Singh, Advocate holding brief of Ms. Anuradha Arora, learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report alleging that the daughter of the informant aged about 16 years was enticed by the applicant, subsequently in the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. the victim has disclosed her age as 19 years and stated that she has gone out of her own free well and they have also married in a Temple.
In the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., there was a slight variance, however, she admitted that she was on talking terms with the applicant.

3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer.

4. Considering the two statements not supporting the prosecution story and the applicant undertaking to get the marriage registered, the applicant who is in custody since 06.06.2024 and has no criminal history is enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

5. Let the applicant Sachin Kumar be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 0155 of 2024, under Sections 363, 366, 323, 506, 376 IPC and Section 3/4 POCSO Act, Police Station Raniganj, District Pratapgarh, on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall get the marriage registered within a period of three months of being enlarged on bail.

(b) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(c) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (d) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
